content: If you are currently taking ranitidine bismuth, it is important to contact your doctor to discuss transitioning to an alternative treatment. Ranitidine bismuth is prescribed to treat intestinal ulcers. It works by combating infections caused by Helicobacter pylori bacteria, which are often associated with ulcers. Treating this infection helps prevent the recurrence of ulcers. This medication is typically used in combination with other drugs. In some cases, it may be prescribed for other purposes; consult your doctor or pharmacist for additional information. Ranitidine bismuth is available in tablet form and is taken orally. It is usually taken twice daily, with or without food. Follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully, and ask your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Take the medication exactly as directed. Do not take more or less than prescribed, and do not take it more frequently than instructed. To fully treat your ulcer, you must use ranitidine bismuth for at least four weeks. Continue taking the medication even if you feel better. Do not stop taking it without consulting your doctor. Before starting ranitidine bismuth, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to ranitidine (Zantac) or any other medications. Provide a list of all prescription and nonprescription medications you are taking, especially aspirin, antacids, and vitamins. Notify your doctor if you have or have ever had kidney, blood, or liver disease. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, inform your doctor. If you become pregnant while taking this medication, contact your doctor immediately. Additionally, let your doctor know if you have previously taken this or any other medication to treat ulcers. If your ulcer symptoms do not improve within the first few days of treatment, inform your doctor, as you may need a different medication. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular dosing schedule. Do not take a double dose to make up for a missed one. Ranitidine bismuth may cause side effects. Temporary darkening of the tongue and stool is harmless. Notify your doctor if any of the following symptoms are severe or persistent: Headache Dizziness Changes in taste perception Constipation Stomach pain If you experience any of the following severe side effects, contact your doctor immediately: Bloody, black, or tarry stools Fever Sore throat Mental confusion Yellowing of the skin or eyes If you experience a serious side effect, you or your doctor can report it to the FDA’s MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program online or by phone. Store this medication in its original container, tightly closed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excessive heat and moisture (do not store it in the bathroom). Dispose of any expired or unused medication properly. Consult your pharmacist for guidance on proper disposal. In case of an overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual collapses or is not breathing, call emergency services at 911. Keep all appointments with your doctor and laboratory. Your doctor may order lab tests to monitor your response to ranitidine bismuth. Do not share this medication with anyone else. If you have questions about refilling your prescription, consult your pharmacist.
